heading: Source
reported_value: Stanford Plasma Physics Laboratory; EM2C CNRS CentraleSupelec; US DOE and Stanford funding; no competing-interest statement
evidence_excerpt_or_description: Taemin Yong, Hongtao Zhong, Erwan Pannier, Christophe Laux and Mark A Cappelli
notes: PDF p. 1 is the IOP cover; printed = PDF - 1; supplementary material (mechanism) not obtained

heading: Electricity supply
reported_value: FID Technology F1112: two opposite-polarity outputs, max 15 kV each (30 kV total), ~10 ns FWHM, 5 ns rise, 30 kHz in all experiments
evidence_excerpt_or_description: The high voltage pulse generator (FID Technology Model F1112) delivers two signals of opposite polarities. Each signal has a maximum value of 15 kV ... The pulse duration is approximately 10 ns (FWHM) ... held constant at 30 kHz
notes: pulser efficiency (wall to load) not reported

heading: Reactor configuration
reported_value: high-pressure chamber (to 125 bar), sapphire windows; inner volume 400 cm3 reduced to 200 cm3 with resin 'as needed for the case of higher pressures'; tungsten pin-to-plane, tip radius ~10 um, gap 150 +/- 30 um
evidence_excerpt_or_description: The inner volume of the chamber, as designed, was 400 cm3, but then reduced to 200 cm3 by filling inert material (resin) to raise the conversion degree of CO above the detection threshold of the GC, as needed for the case of higher pressures
notes: which volume applies to each data set not stated (see E042)

heading: Performance indicators
reported_value: GC (Varian 3400; MS 5A and Porapak Q; TCD and PDHID); compressibility corrected; Phi = x_CO/(x_CO + x_CO2); N_CO ~ 2 N_O2; no other carbon species
evidence_excerpt_or_description: In all conditions studied, GC measurements confirmed that NCO ~ 2NO2

heading: Electricity supply
reported_value: deposited energy per pulse from HV probes (P6015A) and Rogowski coil (Pearson 2877), synchronised to 0.1 ns; e.g. 730 +/- 50 uJ at 5 bar, 20 kV; 95% deposited in the first 7 ns of conduction
evidence_excerpt_or_description: the total energy deposited is measured to be 730 +/- 50 uJ ... A large fraction (95%) of the energy is deposited into the gas within the first 7 ns

heading: Operating conditions
reported_value: carbon deposition and slow electrode degradation; gap 150 -> 250 um after 240 s; pulse energy drifts ~50 uJ in 240 s; fast ablation at too high pressure; stable discharges to 12 bar
evidence_excerpt_or_description: The gap distance was found to increase from the initial 150 um-250 um after 240 s

heading: Performance indicators
reported_value: Phi 14%, eta 23%; p 5.8 bar, E_pulse 700 +/- 75 uJ, tau 420 s
evidence_excerpt_or_description: The highest conversion rate is Phi = 14% and is obtained with an energy efficiency of eta = 23% for the following conditions: p = 5.8 bar, Epulse = 700 +/- 75 uJ, tau = 420 s

heading: Performance indicators
reported_value: eta 27% at Phi 4%; p 5 bar, E_pulse 865 +/- 100 uJ, tau 420 s
evidence_excerpt_or_description: The highest energy efficiency is eta = 27% and is obtained with a conversion rate of Phi = 4% for the following conditions: p = 5 bar, Epulse = 865 +/- 100 uJ, tau = 420 s
notes: inconsistent with its own inputs (C001); Fig. 8b shows ~27% at 120 s, Phi 3.3%

heading: Performance indicators
reported_value: eta = dH/E_CO; E_tot = E_pulse f tau; SEI = E_tot/N0; eta = dH Phi/SEI; N0 from P0, V, Z(P,T0)
evidence_excerpt_or_description: The SEI corresponds to the mean energy used per CO2 molecule that was present initially in the batch reactor

heading: Performance indicators
evidence_excerpt_or_description: Read by eye; text: 'the maximum CO2 conversion is 18%' and 'the energy efficiency slightly drifts from 27% to 22%'

heading: Performance indicators
reported_value: 640 uJ, 400 s, 3.5-12.2 bar: Phi 8% -> 2%, eta ~20% insensitive to pressure
evidence_excerpt_or_description: within 400 s, the conversion degree decreases inversely with pressure, dropping from 8% to 2%, while the energy efficiency is insensitive to pressure, at around 20%

heading: Performance indicators
reported_value: 9 bar, 150 s: Phi rises linearly with pulse energy; eta 16 -> 24% (~330 -> ~920 uJ)
evidence_excerpt_or_description: the conversion degree Phi increases linearly with pulse energy whereas the energy efficiency eta slightly increases, from 16 to 24%

heading: Performance indicators
reported_value: eta ~20% for Phi <15%, weakly sensitive to pressure, pulse energy, time; ~2x previous NRP (Bak et al. 13%); electronic excitation dominates over vibrational
evidence_excerpt_or_description: For conditions where the conversion degree is less than 15%, the energy efficiency is found to be about 20% and exhibits low sensitivity to the pressure, pulse energy, and residence time conditions

heading: Plasma characteristics
reported_value: E/N 660-1100 Td (initial); peak gas temperature ~3000 K per pulse (model), decays within tens of us; n_e 1e17-1e18 cm-3 (model); kernel may exceed CO2 critical pressure above ~10 bar
evidence_excerpt_or_description: The peak temperature reaches ~3000 K due to intensive energy transfer processes in the plasma

heading: Gaps
evidence_excerpt_or_description: eta = Phi x 2.9 eV / (E_pulse f tau / N0), N0 = P V/(Z R T)
notes: headline and 9 bar data fit 200 cm3; 5 bar time series fits 400 cm3

heading: Gaps
normalized_value: the 27% point matches Fig. 8b at 120 s (Phi 3.3%) with V = 400 cm3; the text's 420 s / 865 uJ gives 4-8%
notes: volume per data set not stated; efficiencies of the 5 bar series depend on it by a factor of 2

heading: Performance indicators
normalized_value: EC_CO 1217 kJ/mol = 15.1 kWh/Nm3 (from reported 23%); 1314 kJ/mol = 16.3 kWh/Nm3 (recalc, 200 cm3); 21 W deposited; 48 mmol CO2 per 420 s batch (~0.007 mol/min)
